normal.text: #gamer #artsy So, money is super tight this year, so I’m looking for ways to make little custom things to make the gaming life easier for my RL group. So after buying a bunch of character folios from Ultra-Pro that were on sale, I’m going “How can I make this more awesome?” One of the things my constant consumption of YouTube ttrpg media does is expose me to some ideas, and Mike Ponder, doing a game for the CDProject Red crew introduced standee’s from Monster fight club. normal.name: Elanabelle
normal.text: Retro RPG thought for a Monday evening: Planescape: Torment (1999) lets you talk your way past most of its fights, the final one included. Most games treat conversation as the bit between battles. Torment treats it as the battle. Which old game first made you realise words could be the weapon? #RetroGaming #RPG

normal.name: Felicity Shoulders
normal.text: Anyone know an easy way to set up a free private web-forum these days? I am co-running a mostly online #TTRPG; my co-GM used to set up a ProBoards forum for each long-term campaign. It needs to be something persistent (not a Discord) where players can post game discussion or logs, or even play by post; private to invitees; and obviously since this is a hobby, we prefer free as in beer! I know Obsidian Portal offers forums but only at subscription tier. Any other recs? #rpg #GMing
